Senses.Explanation: In questions about what follows recognition or arrival, “guard and maintain” (保任) asks how something is to be kept in charge over time. The compound occurs 517 times in 180 allowlisted texts, while the question wording “how to guard and maintain?” (如何保任) occurs 158 times in 89. The records preserve sharply different replies. Asked how to guard and maintain from beginning to end, Baizhang Huaihai says, “Like a cattle-herder holding a staff and watching it, not letting it trespass on other people’s seedlings” (如牧牛人執杖視之，不令犯人苗稼). Guizong Zhichang answers, “One film is in the eye; empty flowers fall in confusion” (一翳在眼，空華亂墜). Another record answers the question “How is this matter guarded and maintained?” with “Take care!” (切忌), Deshan Zhixian answers “Guarding and maintaining is itself wrong” (保任即錯), and Qingyuan Weiyin answers Dahui, “Eat when hungry; sleep when tired” (饑來喫飯，困來打眠). A later direct definition by Yongjue Yuanxian says that what he calls guarding and maintaining is “not a fabricated conditioned act” but “nothing more than constantly being alert and not being mixed with ordinary mind” (非假造作有為之法，不過嘗惺惺地，不為凡心所雜而已). The entry reports these attested formulations without making one answer cancel the others.
Senses.Note: This is the primary Chan deployment. “From beginning to end, how to guard and maintain?” (始終如何保任) occurs 12 times in 11 texts, and “throughout the day, how to guard and maintain?” (時中如何保任) occurs 9 times in 9. The lone exact string “guarding and maintaining is itself wrong” (保任即錯) is retained because it is a text-drawn correction to the headword itself.

Occurrences.Kwic: 師曰。未審始終如何保任。百丈曰。如牧牛人執杖視之不令犯人苗稼。師自茲領旨更不馳求。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Jingde Record of the Transmission of the Lamp (景德傳燈錄), Changqing Da'an's biography: Changqing asks how to guard and maintain from beginning to end. Baizhang Huaihai answers with the cattle-herder comparison without repeating the headword; Changqing is the exact questioner.

Occurrences.Kwic: 宗曰。即汝便是。師曰。如何保任。宗曰。一翳在眼空華亂墜
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Jingde Record of the Transmission of the Lamp (景德傳燈錄), Furong Lingxun's biography: Furong asks how to guard and maintain. Guizong Zhichang answers with the mote-in-the-eye line without repeating the headword; Furong is the exact questioner.

Occurrences.Kwic: 問此事如何保任師曰。切忌。問如何是最初一句。師便喝。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Jingde Record of the Transmission of the Lamp (景德傳燈錄), Zizhou Shuilu Heshang section. An unnamed monk asks how to preserve this matter; Shuilu answers, 'strictly avoid it.' The six-rung ladder does not supply the monk's personal name.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Tiansheng Expanded Lamp Record (天聖廣燈錄), Deshan Zhixian entry. Deshan Zhixian is the exact respondent who says that maintaining is itself mistaken; the draft conflated him with the different master Deshan Xuanjian.

Occurrences.Kwic: 慧曰：如何保任？師曰：饑來喫飯，困來打眠。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Complete Book of the Five Lamps, volumes 34–120 (五燈全書(第34卷-第120卷)), in Xin'an Weiyin's biography, identifies Dahui Zonggao as the exact questioner who asks Weiyin how he preserves it; Weiyin answers that he eats when hungry and sleeps when tired.

Senses.Explanation: With a person as beneficiary and a proposition as object, the same compound means “vouch for” or “guarantee.” Damei Fachang assures an unnamed questioner, “I now vouch for this matter for you; it will never be false” (我今為汝保任此事，終不虗也). This denotes an act of assurance rather than continued custody or maintenance, so no single precise English action covers both referents.
Senses.Note: The fuller wording “I now vouch for this matter for you” (我今為汝保任此事) has parallel witnesses in two texts, apparently transmitting the same recorded exchange. It is therefore kept separate but not promoted to an independent multi-source validation.

Occurrences.Kwic: 師云：我今為汝保任此事，終不虗也。僧作禮。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Linked Lamps Compendium (聯燈會要), in the governing Damei Fachang section, identifies Damei Fachang as the speaker who vouches for the matter to an unnamed questioner.
